case_name: Ujjwal Sachdeva & Ors. v. State Of H.P. & Ors.

parties.respondent_defendant: State of H.P., respondent No.1, and others

facts_of_case: FIR sought to be quashed against petitioners-accused under Sections 498-A, 506 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code. Parties have entered into compromise to settle their dispute amicably.

legal_principles.principle: Power under Section 482 Cr.P.C should not be exercised in cases involving heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc.
legal_principles.held: Such offences are not private in nature and have a serious impact on society.
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to prevent abuse of process

legal_principles.principle: The power of the High Court in quashing criminal proceedings or FIR or complaint is distinct and different from the power of a Criminal Court to compound offences under Section 320 Cr.P.C.
legal_principles.held: Even in the judgment passed in Narinder Singh's case, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that while exercising inherent power of quashment under Section 482 Cr.P.C the Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the crime and its social impact.
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — to guide court's exercise of discretion

legal_principles.principle: Criminal proceedings should not be quashed merely on the basis of compromise between the victim and the offender in cases involving heinous and serious offences.
legal_principles.held: Apart from this, offences committed under special statute like the Prevention of Corruption Act or the offences committed by Public Servants while working in that capacity are not to be quashed merely on the basis of compromise between the victim and the offender.
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to prevent abuse of process

outcome.final_order: FIR No.11 of 2024 quashed as parties have resolved to settle their dispute amicably.
